name: MemoTime

paper.title: MemoTime: Memory-Augmented Temporal Knowledge Graph Enhanced Large Language Model Reasoning

construction.unit: experience record: a question decomposition, a seed choice, a toolkit choice, or a solved sub-question with its evidence path
construction.kept_as: structured JSON of the LLM's own reasoning outputs, keyed by the (sub-)question text
construction.processing: after the final LLM sufficiency check says the answer is supported, the decomposition and every freshly retrieved step are written
construction.writer: rule, gated by an LLM sufficiency check (no gold answer)

organization.structure: flat pool of records typed by record kind and temporal question type
organization.stores: one SQLite experience pool + a numpy vector index; the temporal KG is a separate read-only source
organization.index: MiniLM sentence embedding of the query text (paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2)

management.operations: insert, or overwrite the record with the same normalized text; hit counts increase on lookup
management.forgetting: paper: low-value traces pruned and decayed; code: the cleanup function is never called

retrieval.candidates: cosine similarity over records of the same kind (and temporal type)
retrieval.selection: top 10 records for decomposition and toolkit prompts, top 3 for seed choice, similarity threshold 0.1

use.context: retrieved records appear as few-shot examples in the decomposition, seed and toolkit prompts; the answer LLM reads step-by-step evidence from the temporal KG
use.reasoning: Tree of Time: recursive decomposition (depth ≤ 3), toolkit retrieval per sub-question, LLM path choice, debate-vote, sufficiency checks, one final answer call

classify.note: The memory is the experience pool of past reasoning traces. The facts come from a fixed temporal KG, which LLM-chosen toolkits search; that search is not the memory.

stages.ingestion: Test questions arrive one at a time. Question entities are linked to a fixed temporal knowledge graph (MultiTQ: ICEWS05-15; TimeQuestions: Wikidata).
stages.construction: Once the final LLM check accepts an answer, MemoTime writes the question's decomposition and, for each freshly retrieved step, the seed choice, the toolkit choice and the sub-question with its answer and evidence path.
stages.organization: Records form one flat pool typed by record kind and temporal question type, with a sentence-embedding index over the query text.
stages.update: A record with the same normalized text is overwritten, and hit counts grow on lookup. The paper's pruning, decay and cross-type labels are not in the released code.
stages.retrieval: Similar past records (top 10 for decomposition and toolkit choice, top 3 for seeds) become few-shot examples. Evidence itself comes from toolkit searches of the temporal KG, pruned to 80 paths and then to 3 by an LLM.
stages.answer: A final LLM call reads every step's sub-question, chosen answer, evidence path and top candidate paths.

summary: Temporal KGQA agent that splits a question into a tree of time-constrained sub-questions, answers each with operator-specific KG toolkits, and keeps verified decompositions and tool choices as few-shot examples for later questions.
notes: Venue: WWW 2026 (Proceedings of the ACM Web Conference 2026, DOI 10.1145/3774904.3792581), as printed in the arXiv v3 PDF; arXiv comment agrees. The ACM DL page could not be fetched (HTTP 403). Track taken as main (21-page research paper); the PDF does not name a track. Code: SteveTANTAN/MemoTime, pinned at 84ed588 (2026-06-15); Python files last changed 2026-02-18, five days before arXiv v3. DESIGN: §4.1-4.4, App. A (Alg. 1-4), App. D. The experience pool is a store of reasoning traces, not of dialogue or documents; classified as procedural memory. Results: Tables 1-3 in data/results/memotime-2510.13614.json; all baselines copied from earlier papers (App. D).

sources.code_note: HEAD of main (2026-06-15). Its Python files were last changed on 2026-02-18, before arXiv v3 (2026-02-23), so this is taken as the code behind the paper. The repo also ships a pre-filled experience pool (Data/unified_knowledge, 222 records dated 2025-10-01 to 2025-10-11).

abstract.text: MemoTime answers time-sensitive questions over a temporal knowledge graph with an LLM. It breaks a question into a tree of sub-questions whose time constraints must stay consistent, and answers each with toolkits built for specific temporal operators such as 'first after' or 'last before'. Retrieved paths are filtered by time, reranked and narrowed by the LLM. Verified decompositions and tool choices are kept in an experience memory and shown as examples on later questions. The authors report the best results on MultiTQ and TimeQuestions, and say small models such as Qwen3-4B come close to GPT-4-Turbo.
abstract.note: Summary in our words; the original abstract is on arXiv.

headline: The memory holds the system's own past reasoning (decompositions, seed and tool choices), not facts. Facts always come from the temporal KG.
In the released code, stored sub-question answers are never reused: every sub-question searches the KG again, and memory acts only as few-shot examples.
The pool is filled from test questions as the run goes. An LLM check, not the gold answer, decides what is written.

units.name: Experience record
units.role: one reusable piece of past reasoning
units.made_by: rule, after the LLM's final sufficiency check passes

fields.name: query text
fields.what: the question or sub-question, embedded for lookup

fields.name: decomposition
fields.what: sub-questions, indicators, time constraints; shown as an example in the decomposition prompt

fields.name: seed choice
fields.what: sub-question → chosen seed entities; example in the seed prompt (top 3)

fields.name: toolkit choice
fields.what: toolkit, parameters, time hints, reason; example in the toolkit prompt (top 10)

fields.name: sub-question answer
fields.what: entity, time and evidence path of a solved step; written but not read back (reuse branch disabled)

fields.name: type label, hit count
fields.what: temporal question type filter; lookup counter

write.how: LLM (temperature 0) reads all step evidence and says whether the answer is supported
store the question and its sub-question plan
for each step answered by new retrieval, store seed choice, toolkit choice and the sub-question record
a record with the same hash of type + normalized text is overwritten

read.how: keyword rules (after+first, before+last, ...) with an LLM fallback; no memory examples
read.note: paper §4.1 says exemplars from memory guide this step

read.scores: question text vs stored decomposition questions
read.how: LLM writes sub-questions with indicators, given up to 10 similar past decompositions
LLM picks ≤ 3 seed entities (3 examples) and one or more of 8 toolkits (10 examples)
each toolkit expands 1 hop from the seeds under time filters; BGE-M3 dense search adds top 50 facts
sort by time (first/last questions keep the earliest/latest per triple group) or filter by similarity, keep 80
batches of 30 paths; LLM keeps 3 per batch until ≤ 3 remain
debate-vote across toolkit results, then an LLM sufficiency check; if not sufficient: refine, retry or split (depth ≤ 3)

answer_context.format: "Original question" + per step: sub-question, step answer (entity at time), LLM-selected answer and reason, evidence path [heads] - relation - [tails] at time, top 3 candidate paths, toolkit and vote reason
excludes: raw KG neighbourhood beyond the chosen paths
answer_context.note: The returned answer string joins the final LLM answer, the last step's answer and the last chosen entity with ', or ' (stepwise.py L4354-L4364); it is scored by a lenient matcher (substring and word-overlap strategies, answer_verifier.py L466-L532).

compression.what: answer context vs the question's KG neighbourhood
compression.basis: Not reported. The paper gives LLM calls and time per question, not tokens.

paper_vs_code.paper: each node first reuses a matching trace from the pool
paper_vs_code.code: pool_result is hard-coded to None, so every sub-question retrieves anew; stored answers are never read

paper_vs_code.paper: LLM prompt with exemplars retrieved from memory
paper_vs_code.code: keyword rules with an LLM fallback, no memory

paper_vs_code.paper: 0.6·cosine + 0.4·hit count; buffer of 200; question and indicator embeddings
paper_vs_code.code: cosine on question text only; hit count only as a SQL sort in a fallback; buffer 100 and never filled

paper_vs_code.paper: bidirectional BFS up to D_max = 3 hops; semantic-temporal rerank (λ_sem 0.6, exp decay σ)
paper_vs_code.code: 1-hop expansion per toolkit; MAX_DEPTH = 3 is decomposition depth; no BiBFS or σ found; dense rerank disabled

paper_vs_code.paper: obsolete traces pruned; records get secondary type labels
paper_vs_code.code: cleanup_old_entries never called; no secondary labels

open_questions: The w/o-experience-memory ablation (64.2 → 59.8) cannot separate the value of past examples from the order in which test questions filled the pool.
No run compares MemoTime and the baselines with the same backbone except the IO rows in Table 3.

text: Similar past records guide how the question is split and which seeds and toolkits each sub-question uses; the toolkits then search the temporal KG.
Paths are cut to 80 and then 3, voted on and checked; a failed check refines or splits the sub-question, and the final LLM reads every step's evidence.

discussion.takeaway: Time-consistent decomposition plus operator-specific KG toolkits carry most of the gain; the experience memory adds about 4 points on MultiTQ by supplying past plans and tool choices as examples.

claims.claim: State of the art on temporal KGQA, up to 24.0% over the strongest baseline.
claims.evidence: MultiTQ 77.9 vs TempAgent 53.9; TimeQuestions 71.4 vs TimeR4 64.8 (GPT-4-Turbo). Tables 1-2, §5.1

claims.claim: Small models approach GPT-4-Turbo with MemoTime.
claims.evidence: Qwen3-4B 55.3 vs IO 3.5 on MultiTQ (Table 3), against GPT-4-Turbo 76.3. §5.2

claims.claim: Graph retrieval matters most for multi-entity questions.
The question tree is needed for multi-constraint questions.

discussion.limits_src: The paper has no limitations section.
reading: Every baseline number is copied from earlier papers (App. D), mostly with GPT-3.5-Turbo backbones, while MemoTime runs GPT-4o-mini to GPT-4-Turbo; only Table 3's IO rows share a backbone with MemoTime.
Table 3 gives different MemoTime scores than Tables 1-2 for the same backbone (GPT-4-Turbo 76.3 vs 77.9 on MultiTQ, 68.1 vs 71.4 on TimeQuestions); the paper does not explain the gap.
On TimeQuestions the GPT-4o-mini (60.9) and Qwen3-32B (60.6) runs are below the fine-tuned TimeR4 (64.8), so the best result there needs DeepSeek-V3 or GPT-4-Turbo.
In the released code the experience pool only supplies few-shot examples: stored sub-question answers are never reused (stepwise.py L1097), and type classification uses rules, not memory.
The pool is written from test questions during evaluation, gated by an LLM check; results can depend on question order, which the paper does not report.
The code's answer string joins up to three candidate answers with ', or ' and is scored by a lenient matcher, while baselines' Hits@1 comes from their own papers' scoring.
The code skips questions already marked correct for the same configuration on reruns (main.py L252-L260); the paper does not say how many runs produced the tables.
